sections.h2: Which Smithland offices deal with Livingston County property tax?
sections.html:
Livingston County splits the job three ways, and every office is in or near the courthouse square in Smithland. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) fixes each parcel's value. The Livingston County Sheriff, who also handles court security and civil papers, collects the bill. The Livingston County Clerk steps in once a bill is certified as delinquent.

The sheriff's office is at 321 Court Street (PO Box 340, Smithland, KY 42081), answers at 270-928-2122, and opens its doors from 8 to 4 on weekdays. The clerk, at the same street address with a separate box (PO Box 400), takes calls at 270-928-2162 and runs a slightly longer Monday, 8 to 5, and 8 to 4 Tuesday through Friday. The PVA mails from PO Box 77 and lists 270-928-2524 in the state's directory of valuation offices.

Because the PVA does not set rates or take payments, each question has a natural first call. Dispute a value or ask about an exemption with the PVA. Ask about the amount owed or a payoff with the sheriff. Ask about a recorded lien or a tax sale with the clerk.

sections.h2: How do the Census numbers describe a Livingston County house?
sections.html:
Livingston is a small rural market with settled households. The federal QuickFacts table reports the following for 2020-2024 unless noted.

  • The middle owner-occupied home is worth $125,600, and owners live in 81.2 percent of the county's homes.
  • Median gross rent is $926, and median household income is $58,984.
  • One resident in four, 25.1 percent, is 65 or older.
  • The 2020 census counted 8,888 people, and the July 2025 estimate of 8,863 is almost flat.
  • Few people move in a given year, since 93.8 percent stayed at the same address.

Stability like that means listings are few, and buyers often come from nearby Paducah. The county is part of the Paducah metropolitan area, and the Ledbetter community sits directly across the Tennessee River from that city.

sections.h2: What is Livingston County's setting, and how did Smithland start?
sections.html:
The county touches rivers on almost every side. The Ohio River forms its border with Illinois, and the county seat of Smithland sits at the confluence of the Ohio and Cumberland, which is why water covers 8.5 percent of the total area of 342 square miles. Kentucky formed the county in 1798 from Christian County and named it for Robert R. Livingston, a member of the committee that drafted the Declaration of Independence. The county keeps Central time.

Smithland takes its name from John Smith, sent in the late 1790s to scout the river junction for a land company. A plat laid out in 1805 was not recorded until 1837, and the county says that same plat still locates lots in town. The earthquake of December 16, 1811 along the New Madrid Fault shook the river town, and the county's own history page recounts how residents fled into the streets as chimneys fell.

sections.h2: When is the Livingston County tax bill due?
sections.html:
State law gives owners until December 31 of the assessment year, with a discount for early birds. The discount is 2 percent for a full payment made by the first of November. The next two months carry the plain amount, January adds 5 percent, and 10 percent applies after that. If the state approves a late schedule for a county, each stage lasts about a month instead.

The sheriff turns over what remains on April 15. At that point the clerk records the lien, and the debt picks up 1 percent monthly interest. The Department of Revenue's walk-through of a $1,000 bill shows $1,254 at the handoff. Pay in May after a second month of interest and the sample reaches $1,627.61. A buyer at the clerk's sale pays $1,704.21 in the same example, and that figure becomes the base on which the buyer later charges interest and fees.

Before any sale the clerk must run the delinquent list in a newspaper and on a county-sponsored site, and the county attorney mails a 30-day warning to each owner, with a second warning if needed. Ask the Livingston County Clerk for the date of the current sale and for the list of bills certified as delinquent.

sections.h2: How does the PVA arrive at a value, and can a farm owner pay less?
sections.html:
Kentucky recognizes three main methods. For homes the PVA leans on the sales comparison approach, adjusting nearby sales up or down for differences such as a basement. Barns, fences and commercial buildings are valued at replacement cost minus depreciation. Rental properties are valued by the income they produce.

Rural parcels get special treatment. Under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution, farmland is assessed at agricultural value, not market value, so the state's own example taxes an acre that would sell for $50,000 on an agricultural value of $750. The Revenue Department builds per-acre values for cropland, pasture, woodland and waste ground. Ask the PVA whether a parcel is classed as farm use before assuming a market-based figure.

  • Federal, state, county and city property is exempt, as are schools run by nonprofits and religious institutions' buildings and personal property.
  • A nonprofit or religious group applies on Revenue Form 62A023 through the PVA, and a denial can go to the local board.
  • Every parcel gets a physical look from the PVA's staff at least every four years.

sections.h2: How can I appeal a Livingston County assessment?
sections.html:
You have to talk to the PVA first, and the talk has to happen before the inspection period ends. Public viewing of the roll starts the first Monday of May and lasts thirteen days. After your conference, the clerk needs the paperwork by the end of the next workday. The board then sits at the county seat, Smithland, 25 to 35 days later.

Evidence wins or loses these cases. The board considers only what is presented while both sides are in the room, and it denies an appeal that arrives without documents. Photographs of the building, its construction cost, insurance policies, nearby listings and sales all help. A paid representative must hold one of the credentials Kentucky lists, such as attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser, and present your written authorization. If the board changes a value, it must explain why in writing, and a value that rises after bills have printed produces a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: Can Livingston County seniors cut their bill, and what happens at a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. With a quarter of residents past 65, the homestead exemption matters here. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 it removes $49,100 from the assessed value of the owner's home, so a house assessed at $175,000 is taxed on $125,900. Apply through the PVA, bringing a license, birth certificate or passport that proves your age. A buyer cannot inherit the exemption and must file separately.

The year's bill belongs to the person who held title when January 1 arrived, and the closing statement divides the cost. The seller also owes Kentucky's transfer tax under KRS 142.050, $0.50 on each $500 of price, which is collected as the deed is filed in Smithland. Foreclosure transfers and transfers between divorcing spouses are among the exemptions. A delinquent amount stays attached to the property as a lien for up to eleven years, so expect the title agent to want it paid first.

faqs.q: Where is the Livingston County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: Find it at 321 Court Street in Smithland; mail goes to PO Box 340. Call 270-928-2122 on a weekday between 8 and 4.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Livingston County PVA?
faqs.a: The state directory lists 270-928-2524 for the Livingston County PVA, whose mailing address is PO Box 77, Smithland, KY 42081. Call it about values, exemptions and ownership records.

faqs.q: Does Livingston County give a discount for paying early?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the full bill by November 1 and it drops by 2 percent. Past that date you owe the printed amount until year end, and then penalties begin.

faqs.q: What happens to a Livingston County tax bill I never pay?
faqs.a: The sheriff sends it to the clerk after April 15, and a lien goes on record with interest and commissions piling up. Investors may buy the debt at a sale a few months later.

faqs.q: Is farmland taxed differently in Livingston County?
faqs.a: Yes. Kentucky assesses farmland at agricultural value rather than market value, using per-acre figures for cropland, pasture and woodland. Ask the PVA whether your acreage qualifies as farm use.
